reviews.comment: Great professor, make sure to pay attention to what he goes over in lectures as it shows up in exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: VERY LENIENT Grader and very easy class. His material is very straightforward and the exams are close to the notes. He's pretty quiet, and thinks we know more than we do. He gives a bank of questions 25-30/150ish given per exam to review for the exam, and about 90% of it is on the exam itself. Average lecturer, easy class.
Very simple and trivial. Don't take the course tho.

If given the choice, I would not retake the class with this professor, but he was not the worst ever. Definitely get ready to read the textbook and make sure you go over the reviews he gives before exams. Easily passable if you study and put in the work.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'll start by saying the class itself is not bad, test is SUPER close to the reviews he gives, an A is achievable if you try. Teaching wise, sub par, lectures are hard to follow, slides are overwhelming and not appealing. He is a nice guy and the grader is SUPER lenient on tests. "Trivial" is a buzz word.

Awful lectures & slides. Most of what he talks about in lecture is way to complicated and has nothing to do with that's on the actual exam. Slides are terribly formatted, VERY CHAOTIC, and very difficult to follow.
Exams however are easy - he sends out review problems and the exam consists of problems pulled directly from the review.
He's nice tho
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awful professor, the slides for his lectures are simultaneously archaic and chaotic, making it a difficult read. He emphasizes reading the textbook before lecture, but almost nothing covered in his slides is actually in the textbook. The only saving grace is the fact that the tests are not too difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kocharovsky's lectures were very monotone, unorganized, often off-topic, and difficult to follow. Better off just reading the textbook and reviewing the topics outside of class if you actually want to learn and do well.
I learned nothing from this class. He doesn't teach at all. It was a massive, very stressful waste of my time.

He is a super caring guy and a very easy grader, for a physics class it is very easy, and the tests are mostly made up of memorized derivations. There are lots of I-clicker pop quizzes that are generally very doable.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Kocharovsky is the best choice for Physics 221 at A&M. His lectures are interesting and easy to understand and the tests are pretty doable. Lectures involve lots of sample problems which are similar to exam questions. Dr. Kocharovsky is easy to contact and understanding if students have problems.

This professor was a terrible choice for teaching this class in my opinion. He seems very nice, and is clearly highly intelligent, but for a class meant to be the first class in which physics majors learn separately from all other majors he is highly unorganized and instills a deep sense of overwhelming dread about the field and the class content.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you've taken physics before, then go for it. He is super funny and fosters a relaxed class environment. However, if it's your first time taking physics, do not expect to learn much; his lectures are helplessly unorganized. This man is the most dedicated and humble person you could ever meet.

He is very smart when it comes to physics but is a very bad professor as his lecture slides are very messy and his handwriting and voice are hard to understand at times. Invest in spartan tutoring for the week before the exam to learn all the material or if possible take Ali Kaya.

This man is so beyond 206, it's the equivalent of us trying to teach 3-year-olds the alphabet. He is very soft-spoken and has an accent that is muffled by his KN95, but he is such a sweet guy who really does want to see you succeed. His slides are daunting, but the textbook, *CQ*, HW & previous exams are where you will do most of your learning.

He is so smart, but he should be teaching higher level physics. I feel bad that he is wasting his knowledge on freshman. Stopped going to lectures after first test and did clickers remotely because it was a better use of my time to learn the material myself. If you are weak in physics, take another professor because you won't learn from him.
i made a bingo in his class to keep myself entertained. Nice guy, but doesn't know how to teach. Attendance mandatory due to iclickers.

Your experience in your phys206 lecture will be determined by the professor you have. This professor ain't it. Slides are awful, jumbled, and confusing, and he speaks through a microphone, with a thick accent, and a heavy mask on. I always joked with my classmates: "I'm sure what he's saying is worth listening to. I just can't hear it."

Failed this class by 5 points, attended every lecture but I didn't learn a single thing from him. He seems like a great guy, but he knows too much and he overcomplicates the content so much, it's hard to learn anything if this is your first time taking physics like it was for me. Had to read every page of the textbook and it still wasn't enough.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not the best professor, to say the least. His lectures were difficult to follow along with, but you have to attend them because of the iClicker questions. The good thing about taking the class with him is that you'll be doing University Physics and not Don't Panic, meaning tests will be easier.

The professor was hard to comprehend, not only because of the accent, but because he frequently mumbles. His slides are incredibly disorganized. The numbers and words often overlap each other, and every space in a slide is terribly filled up. They are legible to no one. He does not respond to emails. He messes up iclickers and does not fix them.

Professor Kocharovsky is very passionate about the subject of physics which is nice to see. Still, due to his accent and horrible organization on his lecture slides, the class was very hard for someone like me who has not taken physics before. Spartan Tutoring's online archive for phys206 was well worth the money and was likely the reason I passed.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a student who is coming in with AP Physics C credit, this class is far easier than my experience in high school. The problems are directed towards students with no physics knowledge at all, so for those who have taken physics before, the material is slowly paced. This class uses an online textbook with hours of homework. Professor is nice too!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Kocharovsky gets a lot of hate he doesn't deserve. Easily one of the nicest professors I have ever had and he truly does care about his students. It may be a bit difficult to understand him at first because he has a thick accent, but you get used to it. Definitely recommend going to his office hours because he is nice and will help.

Phys 206 by nature is a pretty difficult class and regardless of your professor you will need to put in a lot of work outside of class to do well. Dr. Kocharovsky's slides are very messy and a lot of his lectures are not that helpful, however his reviews before the test are super helpful in preparing for the exam.

Kocharovsky is one of the greatest minds in theoretical physics. Success depends on your effort.Take advantage of the resources provided. Don't play chess during lecture. Lecture may be challenging, so reinforce with the textbook. Do not be initmidated by his accent! He's more than willing to help those who approach him. Highly recommend!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Kocharovsky is a nice man who does want to help you, but is not a good prof. Very hard to understand his thick russian accent and he wears a mask which makes it even worse. Powerpoints are too crammed and tests are 80% of the grade. You teach yourself everything. Don't take him.
I got an A, but it was literally all self taught. His lectures were completely useless. So if you want some help so your not teaching yourself everything, choose someone else

Please don't take Kocharovky. 

His lectures are useless. His slides are CRAMMED with waaaay too much information (not to mention, often irrelevant information). His accent can be difficult to understand, especially in the first few weeks of classes. I didn't put the effort in I should have, but that doesn't deny that he was a terrible prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: First time taking physics? You'll struggle. His lectures are dense and hard to understand with his accent + mask. I had to teach myself from the textbook. Luckily, the backwards way that University Physics grades exams helps in the long run. I definitely recommend getting outside tutoring or help if you don't understand the material.

Prof. Kocharovsky is brilliant, but this interferes with his ability to teach. He has a thick Russian accent and teaches basic concepts way too far in-depth that makes it very difficult to understand. I would not recommend him because I found his lectures super cluttered and useless. Homework is hard and doesn't teach you much. DO PRACTICE EXAMS!!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take Vitaly, he strikes me as a chill dude and he's certainly a genius, but my gosh you won't learn a thing from the man. Slides will give you a seizure trying to read them and it's just basically impossible to learn anything from class. If you put in the work, you can probably make an A in 206 regardless, but I would not recommend Vitaly.

He has Russian accent, iclicker, textbook is for online homework, the exams are weird for this class, your exam grade is 80% but you can fix or undo objects every test, its multiple choice so you get partial credit for guessing an answer close I didnt go to class I did clicker remotely and went to a diff prof, Dawson Nodurft. He rounded my grade up

He is definitely knowledgeable in physics, but it is so hard to understand him and his lecture slides are a mess. He is super helpful though, I was struggling and he gave me an extension on my homework that I didn't do to help me raise my grade. Overall he is very understanding and a very nice guy!

Do not undertake Kockarovsky or University Physics for 206. If you have not taken the class in high school you will struggle. Konchalovsky has a very thick Russian accent, so if you struggle to understand accents, make sure to consider this. I could understand his accent but still found listening to his lectures to cause more harm than good.

He says you should spend ten hours a day studying for school. That's 70 hrs/week. 8 hrs sleep per night and there's another 56 hours. 42 hours left per week and I have to work full time. No showers yet, no eating, no commute, etc. His accent is very strong and very hard to understand. He's a genius but he should be in a lab not a classroom.

Perhaps it was the online setting, but it just didn't work. Thankfully, I had a great high school professor. Laughably, unimaginably awful lecture slides. Lots of clickers. Just a very tedious and stressful class, as I had to teach all of it to myself, the lectures felt useless. Seems like a nice guy though, definitely very smart. Exams are 80% btw
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Kocharovsky is a smart guy and I bet he's a nice person but his class was awful. I had little physics knowledge coming into college and had to put in an insane amount of outside work to barely pass the class. His slides are jumbled and he has a thick accent. The exams are insanely difficult and are worth 80% of your total grade. Do not take him
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He has a heavy accent and his ppt are very disorganized. You have to have previous knowledge of what he teachers or you will suffer.

Physics is already bad as it is, but online even worse. Professor is a nice guy and super smart, but I could not understand a thing going on in lecture. The slides were all over the place and I was teaching myself. Very thick Russian Accent and hard to understand. I respect the guy, but I would not recommend taking physics 206 with him.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures will do nothing for you. It honestly helped my grade when I stopped trying to understand his lectures and just took notes over the prelecture videos. He is really understanding though and a lot more organized than other university physics professors. I would definitely take him over Saslow.

The man is smart don't get me wrong, but he just cannot teach. Apart from his heavy Russian accent, he overcrowds his slides and mumbles when presenting them. Being an online class didn't help anything either; he will give out Clicker quizzes and then wonders why 40% of the class got the answer. Gives little time for questions. Would not recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures overcomplicate everything with overcrowded powerpoint slides. It's very difficult to follow his powerpoints and work, but attendance is mandatory. Had I not taken mechanics in high school, I likely would've failed this class.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hes an ok teacher but his accent is hard to understand and his powerpoints are a mess. The class is really hard for any professor so its not like its his fault. Clicker worth 5% so go to class.

Literally the worst possible prof you could choose for phys 206. This man is a genius but can't explain anything at all. If that doesn't scare you, you can't even understand his terrible explinations because of his insanely thick russian accent. His powerpoint slides give me a seizure they look like a 2 year old einstein's coloring book.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Kocharovsky is actually a great professor but he doesn't do the best job in class about explain things he thinks are simple, if you go to his office hours, he is incredibly useful and helpful about trying to help you understand topics, and he does actually care for his students
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The only reason I earned an A is because of teaching myself physics. This professor just did not work for me. He is very smart and definitely knows what he is talking about, but the lectures are SO confusing & all over the place w/ messy examples. I usually tried to pay attention but after 10 minutes I was zoned out or falling asleep. Good luck.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Phys 206 is a very hard class regardless of your professor. Kocharovsky is a caring professor and wants his students to do well. However, if you like learning concepts first then going into the math then he may not be for you. He would do math proofs before explaining the concepts so I was very lost and quickly lost interest in the class

It was very difficult to determine what this professor was trying to convey in his lectures. There are iClicker quizzes every time you have a class which is worth 5% of your grade overall. My best advice is to take the practice exams from the previous semesters before each exam. These were more useful than any lecture or homework assignment.

A lot of people don't like Dr. Kocharovsky, but I am a huge fan. The man is an awesome guy, the class is hard, but that isn't his fault, all of the 206 classes are the same. The clicker questions are pretty bad though, and be prepared to do poorly on them.

This professor is my man. He genuinely cares about your learning and doing well in the class. All you have to do is go up and talk to him. He is the friendliest professor I have met at Texas A&M. He is also extremely smart. I've personally asked him about many advanced topics in physics with him and he has never stumbled.

A lot of students complain about his accent, but if you actually paid attention instead of watching Netflix or talking to friends, you would understand every thing he says. Kocharovsky is so knowledgeable and nice. His exam review sessions were so helpful (gave examples of problems on the test). His demonstrations were always funny.
Dr. Kocharovsky is one of the best teachers I have ever had.

Dr. Kocharovsky is one of the best professors I have had at A&M. He is absolutely brilliant, and his lectures are entertaining. His teaching relies heavily on enabling students to develop a sound intuition for topics in the course and deriving proper equations used when solving problems. He is very caring and wants to see all his students succeed.

Vitaly is super Russian, but you'll get used to the Soviet accent after awhile. Really knows what he's talking about, but lecture slides are really messy and hard to decipher. He cares about his students, and he isn't as ridiculous as everyone makes him out to be.

I see Vitaly Kocharovsky as the grandpa of the A&M campus. When he is not teaching, I feel as if we would kick back in his office and crush a thirty rack. When given the aux, he spits fire. He is the guy you pass the ball to make the game winning three. He is my spirit animal.

I thought he was a decent professor, although he definitely had some shortcomings. Many people struggled to understand him due to his thick accent. His slides were also very crammed, many people had difficulty understanding them. He was very accessible outside of class, he definitely seemed to care about the success of his students.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: lecture slides are next level terrible. the class was truly traumatizing experience. would never recommend. nice guy though
By far one of the worst experiences that I've had was taking Physics 218 with him.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There is no good 218 prof but all are better than him. His lectures make you more confused that when you come in from his theoretical applications examples that aren't on the test. His slides are awful. A+ is the only way I understood the class and my TA was great help. Seriously though, Russian to the bone and has the thickest accent in the world.

He's a very interesting guy when he tells stories about the revolution in Russia and aliens but he can't explain basic physics because he does quantum. His lecture slides will hurt your eyes with the different colors and crammed information, you will fall asleep, and clicker questions are at the end of class

His accent makes class pretty difficult on top of physics already being a difficult subject. He has a bad habit of turning toward the board and speaking quietly while he's writing, so you have to ask him to turn around and raise his voice. He's very knowledgable, but has a hard time delivering the subject. I would not recommend.

Koch is a very interesting prof. His lectures are very long and boring and his accent makes it harder to pay attention. He was not very helpful when I had questions so I depended heavily on my recitation leader. That being said, he will give you points back on your exams if you go in and review them with him- which helped a lot.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Put a 0 for all the webassign lab blanks except for where it asks for time (put any number) and you will finish the lab in seconds.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Taking this prof was an experience to say the least. While he did seem like a genuinely good guy, he could not teach American students physics to save his life. Once you finally understand what he's trying to say through his thick Russian accent, you're only halfway there. Physics is hard alone, & physics at TAMU is even worse. You've been warned.

He can be hard to understand at times, but you can tell he really wants you to understand physics.   He also does give reviews about what is going to be on the exam.  He's really nice and is definitely passionate about physics.  218 is hard whoever your prof is, so you're going to have to study a lot.  Dr. Kochoravsky is a pretty cool prof.

Grading is really weird for the course, but its not the professor's fault. Dr. Kocharovsky is brilliant and really wants the students to do well and understand. His lecture slides are filled with information but if you pay attention in class, its easy to follow. The lab/recitation for this course is horrible and a waste of time.

Tough class. He is a SUPER smart professor. His lecture slides are jam packed with information, but if you pay attention he will tell you exactly what to know for tests. Attendance is not mandatory but there are iClicker questions in each class. He reviews before each test and it helps a lot. He wants you to do well in the class.

He has an extremely thick Russian accent that's somehow still understandable, even though he sounds like he has a buttermilk biscuit stuffed into his mouth at all times. His PowerPoint presentations are also extremely cluttered.
For people who find physics difficult don't take this class. Has a thick Russian Accent so it's hard to follow at times

Dr. Kocharovsky is not the easiest professor but he does have his benefits. He is incredibly helpful during office hours but his lectures are occasionally irrelevant in terms of the common exam. His final was easy because he gave us a list of 20 problems prior to the final, and chose 5 of them for the actual test.

It's true that his lectures aren't the best. I taught myself the material and got an A. He likes students who work hard, and he will give back points on tests afterwards, if you go to his office hours and make a good case for yourself.        Also, he exempted some students from the final exam, students who did well on the physics challenge exam.

From my review, it seems like he's a bad professor, but he's not. He could do better presenting the information, but I honestly learned better from the textbook, and going to class didn't really help my understanding. He's there for you if you need the help, but sometimes it's still confusing. I ended up with a B, but I was never good at physics.

Although he is a brilliant individual, in my opinion Vitaly is the worst physics professor at A&M. His lectures are impossible to understand, and he teaches 3 chapters ahead of every other professor. In other words, each exam covers material you were supposed to have learned 3 weeks ago while he lecture over the next set of chapters. Do not take.

He has terribly strong accent, which makes his lectures almost pointless. If you go to his office hours he will go over anything you'd like and that is probably your best best. The common tests are impossible since he doesn't teach much, but his final was very easy since he put it together himself.

He has a very think Russian accent. Extremely smart man, but he says everything is "trivial" instead of teaching it. The only reason I passed this class was because of tutoring. Office hours aren't even helpful, and forget trying to learn from his power points.

Horrible teacher, He has the among the worst test averages among all physics classes, and says everything "is trivial" Half the class does homework for another class during his lectures while the other half that listens claim to come out more confused than they went in. maybe 35% of students Q dropped him. The only reason Ill pass is  self taught.
